title: This 240Z Asks: Restomod or Restoration?

body_markdown:
A significant portion of the collector car market seeks out completely unrestored vehicles in pristine condition. Folks in this realm are willing to pay quite a bit to get cars just as they were when they rolled off the assembly line. For them, the guiding principle is, “it’s only original once.” Other buyers don’t mind a restoration that sticks as closely as possible to the original formula, with new replica parts that duplicate the original specs. For any car that’s seen decades of use, this is often the next best thing to driving an all-original model. In yet another category are those that don’t care for originality at all. These car lovers know that mass-produced cars are the result of all kinds of compromises, and there are many ways to improve the looks, engine performance, ride quality, or audio system, just to name a few. This group of car lovers includes everyone from[OEM-Plus](https://www.hagerty.com/media/tags/oem-plus/) aficionados to wild customizers.


Marketplace/GPA-Shadow


Marketplace/GPA-Shadow


When it comes to buying and selling a modified car, the quality and type of modification matter. Just about all buyers are interested in a well-kept classic that’s original or close to it. The further the car gets from its original look and performance, the narrower the buyer pool gets. However, we’ve seen plenty of high-end restomods command far more than a comparable car in #1(Concours) condition. We’ve noted—[several times](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/hagerty-insider/c2-stock-v-restomod/) — that ‘50s and[‘60s Corvette buyers are willing to pay top dollar for the right highly customized models](https://www.hagerty.com/media/buying-and-selling/auctions/13-customized-midyear-corvettes-soared-over-250k-this-january/) .


This 1971 Datsun 240Z—[up for auction on Hagerty Marketplace](https://www.hagerty.com/marketplace/auction/1971-Datsun-240Z/cbc5034f-250c-4d8c-8d13-fba560675532) —is a good example of a mild restomod that might have the right combination of upgrades to make it approachable for a lot of buyers. It has several upgrades, although they all add up to a desirable package. Importantly, it looks ready to hit the road.


Marketplace/GPA-Shadow


Datsun got the exterior styling of the original Z car on the first try. There’s not much worth changing there. This one took a stealthy approach with a repaint in Spiral Gray Metallic, a factory color for C5 Corvettes, along with blacked-out brightwork. Covering up chrome might be a dealbreaker for many buyers, although it works rather well with the overall look of the car, which also features Japanese-market taillights and fender-mounted mirrors.


In keeping with the charcoal and black theme, 16-inch Minilite-style wheels were coated to match the car.


Marketplace/GPA-Shadow


While the interior looks restored, there are plenty of hidden upgrades to the drivetrain and chassis. The 2.4-liter inline six breathes through an exhaust header and relies on an electric fuel pump and an electric cooling fan, the latter of which pulls air through a more modern aluminum radiator. A four-speed transmission sends power to a Nissan R200 differential with 3.90:1 gears, offering both improved strength and 16% more torque multiplication. Helping with the right stance and improved handling, the suspension was lowered with Eibach springs, and each corner uses disc brakes and KYB shocks. Stiffer anti-sway bars have been fitted at both ends.


The twin one-barrel SU carbs were replaced with a pair of Weber-style downdraft carbs.


Marketplace/GPA-Shadow


The market for 1971 240Zs has softened significantly in the last five years.[Values are down from last quarter, erasing almost all of the gains made in 2025.](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/datsun/240z/1971/1971-datsun-240z-base?id=aCn1I000000DIqLSAW&timeframe=5Y) Still, these beautiful coupes are appreciated by a big segment of the collector market. There’s plenty of time left in this auction. We’ll be watching to see how it stacks up against its unmodified counterparts.
